questions.q: A system of government in which the executive and legislature are fused and the executive stays in office only while it retains the confidence of the legislature is called
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system the prime minister and cabinet are drawn from and accountable to the legislature, and a vote of no confidence can remove them. A presidential system separates the executive from the legislature, while a confederal system concerns the relationship between central and component states.

questions.q: The National Association of Nigerian Students organises a radio campaign and peaceful march in Abuja in support of a bill on student loans. This activity best illustrates
questions.explanation: Pressure groups and citizens can shape government decisions by informing and persuading the public; the radio campaign and march are ways of mobilising public opinion. Judicial review is a court function, legislative oversight is performed by the legislature, and collective responsibility concerns cabinet solidarity.

questions.q: A political arrangement under which military rulers and civilian politicians jointly exercise governmental power is called
questions.explanation: Diarchy describes a sharing of governing power, such as the military–civilian arrangement during some Nigerian military regimes. Oligarchy is rule by a small group, plutocracy is rule by the wealthy, and gerontocracy is rule by elders.

questions.q: Nigeria signs a defence pact with another state and later withdraws from it without seeking permission from any foreign authority. This action best illustrates the exercise of
questions.explanation: External sovereignty is the independence of a state in its relations with other states, including the power to enter or withdraw from treaties. Internal sovereignty concerns supremacy within the state's own territory, while legitimacy is acceptance of a government's right to rule and delegated legislation is subordinate law-making.

questions.q: A newly elected governor in a Nigerian state enjoys legitimacy mainly because
options: he was installed by a group of influential traditional rulers
most citizens accept the administration as having the right to govern after a credible election
his posters and campaign billboards are the most visible in the state
he has the ability to use force against anyone who opposes his policies
questions.explanation: Legitimacy means that citizens generally accept a government's right to rule. The ability to use force shows power or coercion, campaign visibility does not by itself show acceptance, and traditional endorsement alone does not confer constitutional legitimacy on a state government.

questions.q: A teacher in a secondary school in Enugu gives a directive to students, and they comply because the school rule book empowers the teacher to do so. This compliance is based mainly on
questions.explanation: Authority is the recognised right to give commands and be obeyed, which here comes from the school rule book. Coercion involves threats or force, while influence rests on persuasion or personal effect rather than formal rules; sovereignty belongs to the state.

questions.q: The Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, is administered by an authority under the control of the
questions.explanation: The Constitution places the Federal Capital Territory under federal executive authority, exercised through a minister appointed by the President. Abuja Municipal Area Council is only a local council within the territory, while the National Assembly makes laws for the territory but does not administer it day-to-day.

questions.q: A state government in Nigeria uses its monthly statutory allocation mainly for the payment of salaries and provision of infrastructure. Such allocation is received from the
questions.explanation: Statutory allocations are the state's share of revenue distributed from the Federation Account by the Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission. The State Joint Local Government Account is for local councils, the Ecological Fund addresses special ecological problems, and the Board of Internal Revenue collects state internal revenue.

questions.q: The organ of the United Nations in which every member state has one vote is the
questions.explanation: In the General Assembly, each member state has one vote, making it the most representative UN organ. The Security Council has limited membership with permanent members holding veto power, the International Court of Justice consists of judges, and the Economic and Social Council has limited elected membership.

questions.q: The headquarters of the African Union is located in
questions.explanation: The African Union has its headquarters in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. Abuja hosts the ECOWAS Commission, while Nairobi hosts several UN bodies; Accra is not the seat of the African Union.

questions.q: The emphasis in Nigeria's foreign policy on attracting foreign investment and promoting trade is best described as
questions.explanation: Economic diplomacy uses diplomatic channels to promote trade, investment and the economic interests of a country. Non-alignment concerns Cold War bloc politics, pan-Africanism prioritises African unity and cooperation, and collective security involves joint action against aggression.

questions.q: The primary objective of a political party, unlike that of a pressure group, is to
options: educate the public on national issues
influence government policy on particular issues
contest elections and form the government
protect the professional interests of its members
questions.explanation: A political party is organised mainly to contest elections and take control of government, whereas a pressure group seeks to influence policy without necessarily seeking office. Protecting professional interests and focusing on particular policy issues are typical pressure-group aims; public enlightenment can be carried out by both.

questions.q: A trade union in Enugu submits a memorandum to the National Assembly opposing a proposed tax law that would affect workers. This action best illustrates the pressure group function of
questions.explanation: Submitting a memorandum to lawmakers to express workers' concerns is a form of interest articulation, by which a pressure group makes its members' interests known to government. It is not political recruitment, electioneering or policy implementation.

questions.q: A political party in which a few leaders select candidates for elections without holding primaries is said to lack
questions.explanation: When party leaders choose candidates without primaries or popular participation, the party is lacking internal democracy. Party manifesto, cross-carpeting and electoral mandate refer to different concepts.

questions.q: One major strength of proportional representation compared with the first-past-the-post system is that it
options: makes the number of seats won by a party broadly reflect its share of the votes
reduces the cost and complexity of conducting elections
guarantees that every elected member has a direct constituency link with voters
always produces a single-party majority government quickly
questions.explanation: Proportional representation allocates seats in close proportion to the votes won by each party, making the result fairer to smaller parties. A direct constituency link and simple, cheap elections are usually associated with first-past-the-post rather than proportional representation. Proportional representation can also make coalition governments more common.

questions.q: In a public opinion poll, the use of a random sample is important mainly because it
options: ensures that the views of every adult in the country are collected individually
makes the result of the poll automatically decide the next election
gives every member of the target population a chance of being selected, thereby reducing bias
guarantees that every respondent will give an honest answer
questions.explanation: A random sample gives members of the target population a chance of selection, so the poll is less likely to be skewed towards one group. It does not mean that every adult is interviewed individually, nor does it guarantee honest answers. A public opinion poll measures opinion but does not decide or conduct elections.

questions.q: Which of the following is a civic duty rather than a fundamental right of a Nigerian citizen?
questions.explanation: Civic duties are responsibilities that citizens owe to the state, such as paying taxes and obeying the law. Freedom of expression, fair hearing and freedom of movement are constitutionally guaranteed fundamental rights. They protect the individual rather than impose an obligation on the citizen.

questions.q: A constitutional government is best described as a government in which
options: the constitution is always unwritten and flexible
political power is exercised according to established laws that limit the powers of rulers
the ruler is above the law during a state of emergency
the legislature has unlimited power over all other institutions
questions.explanation: Constitutional government means limited government in which rulers exercise power according to law and the constitution. It is not defined by having only an unwritten constitution, and it does not permit any institution or ruler to be above the law. Unlimited legislative power or emergency rule above the law contradicts constitutionalism.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: The power of a court to declare an executive action unconstitutional is an example of
options: a legislative check on the judiciary
a federal check on state governments
a judicial check on the executive
an executive check on the judiciary
questions.explanation: Judicial review allows the courts to examine executive actions and declare them invalid if they conflict with the constitution. This is a judicial check on the executive, not the executive or legislature checking the courts. It is also different from a federal-state power relationship.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: The main purpose of checks and balances in a presidential constitution is to
options: make the three arms of government perform the same functions
ensure that the executive always controls the legislature
allow judges to make laws whenever the legislature is slow
prevent any one branch of government from becoming too powerful
questions.explanation: Checks and balances allow each branch of government to limit the powers of the other branches, thereby reducing the risk of tyranny. Separation of powers assigns different functions to the branches rather than making them perform the same functions. The executive is not meant to control the legislature permanently.

questions.q: The mass media influence public opinion mainly by
options: preventing the government from making any unpopular policy
replacing the family and school as agents of socialisation
compelling citizens to vote for a particular candidate
selecting, interpreting and giving prominence to issues and events
questions.explanation: The mass media shape public opinion through agenda-setting and framing, that is, by deciding which issues to highlight and how to present them. They may influence voters, but they do not compel people to vote for a particular candidate. They also do not replace the family and school or completely prevent government policies.

questions.q: Under the 1963 Republican Constitution, the President of Nigeria was elected by
options: registered voters in the four regions
members of both Houses of the Federal Parliament
questions.explanation: Under the 1963 Republican Constitution, the President was a ceremonial Head of State chosen by members of both Houses of the Federal Parliament. The Prime Minister continued to exercise executive power.

questions.q: Under the 1979 Constitution, a candidate for President was required to obtain at least one-quarter of the votes cast in each of at least
questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution required a presidential candidate to have the highest number of votes and at least one-quarter of the votes cast in each of at least two-thirds of the states. At that time, two-thirds of the 19 states meant at least 13 states.

questions.q: The Ooni of Ife is widely obeyed by many traditional title holders in Yorubaland because of the age-long customs and beliefs surrounding the stool. This form of authority is best described as
questions.explanation: Following the stool because of inherited custom and belief is traditional authority, which rests on accepted historical practice. Legal-rational authority rests on formal office and rules, while charismatic authority rests on personal qualities.

questions.q: The capacity of a state to enter into treaties and conduct relations with other states without external dictation is best described as
questions.explanation: External sovereignty refers to a state’s independence from external control and its capacity to deal with other states in its own right. Internal sovereignty concerns supremacy within the state’s territory, not the conduct of foreign relations.

questions.q: Under the 1999 Constitution, a matter that appears only in the Exclusive Legislative List can be legislated upon by
options: only the State House of Assembly
the local government council of the area concerned
both the National Assembly and State Houses of Assembly
questions.explanation: The Exclusive Legislative List is reserved for the National Assembly; state houses cannot legislate on it unless the Constitution provides otherwise. Matters on the concurrent legislative list may be legislated on by both levels, but this matter is not on that list.

questions.q: In the United Nations Security Council, the power of veto is held by
options: all fifteen members of the Council
questions.explanation: Only the five permanent members—China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States—hold veto power in the Security Council. Non-permanent members and the General Assembly do not exercise this veto.

questions.q: The African Union was established in 2002 to replace the
options: United Nations Economic Commission for Africa
Economic Community of West African States
questions.explanation: The African Union was launched in 2002 as a successor to the Organisation of African Unity, which had been founded in 1963. ECOWAS is a West African regional body, not the organisation replaced by the AU.

questions.q: The ECOWAS Court of Justice has its headquarters in
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS Court of Justice is based in Abuja, Nigeria, where it hears disputes concerning ECOWAS law and related matters. Its seat should not be confused with the locations of other regional institutions.

questions.q: Nigeria sends a trade delegation to Accra to negotiate better access for made-in-Nigeria cement and to attract Ghanaian investors into the Lekki Free Zone. This action best illustrates the foreign policy objective of
questions.explanation: Economic diplomacy uses diplomatic contacts to promote trade, investment and other economic interests abroad. Collective security concerns joint action against aggression, while decolonisation and non-alignment relate to independence struggles and Cold War neutrality respectively.

questions.q: The Nigerian Bar Association issues a communiqué condemning delays in the administration of justice and submits proposals to the National Assembly, but it does not sponsor candidates for election. This action is best classified as the method of a
questions.explanation: A pressure group seeks to influence government policy without contesting elections to capture power. A political party, by contrast, sponsors candidates for election, while a judicial tribunal and an electoral commission perform different statutory functions.

questions.q: A bill passed by the National Assembly is returned by the President with a memorandum giving reasons why he will not sign it. This action is an exercise of the power of
questions.explanation: The President may withhold assent to a bill, and the National Assembly can later override that decision by a two-thirds majority in each chamber. Dissolution and a vote of no confidence are not powers exercisable in this manner, while the prerogative of mercy concerns punishment after conviction.

questions.q: The 1999 Constitution provides that if any other law is inconsistent with its provisions, the Constitution shall prevail and the other law shall be void to the extent of its inconsistency. This provision establishes
questions.explanation: The provision places the Constitution above every other law, so any inconsistent law is invalid to the extent of the conflict. This is different from parliamentary supremacy, where the legislature is the highest legal authority, and it does not by itself describe judicial independence or collective responsibility.

questions.q: A political party is performing the function of interest aggregation when it
options: conducts primary elections to choose its candidates
prints and distributes membership cards to new supporters
holds a rally to explain its policies to the electorate
brings together the demands of farmers, teachers and traders into a common manifesto
questions.explanation: Interest aggregation involves combining varied demands from different groups into a coherent party programme. Printing membership cards is a membership drive, conducting primaries is candidate selection, and holding a rally is mainly political education and mobilisation.

questions.q: A serving member of the House of Representatives who is appointed as a minister is required to resign his legislative seat before taking office. This requirement best illustrates the principle of
questions.explanation: Separation of powers keeps the personnel and functions of the legislature and executive distinct, so the same person does not simultaneously serve in both branches. Collective responsibility concerns joint ministerial accountability, federal character concerns balanced representation, and parliamentary supremacy concerns legislative dominance.

questions.q: A constitution whose main rules are found in statutes, judicial decisions and conventions rather than in a single document is best described as
questions.explanation: An unwritten constitution is not codified in one document but is found in several sources, including statutes, court decisions and conventions. It may still contain written laws, but it is not consolidated into a single constitutional text.

questions.q: One major source of public criticism of General Yakubu Gowon's military administration before 1975 was its
options: delay in fixing and keeping a timetable for returning to civilian rule
abolition of the federal system of government
refusal to create any state in Nigeria
questions.explanation: Critics accused Gowon's government of failing to provide a clear and credible programme for civilian rule, especially after 1970. The regime did not abolish the federal system; in fact, it created states in 1967.

questions.q: In a local government election in Ogun State, 120,000 voters were registered. A total of 105,000 votes were cast, of which 5,000 were invalid. Candidate A scored 45,000 valid votes. What percentage of the valid votes did Candidate A obtain?
questions.explanation: Valid votes cast = 105,000 − 5,000 = 100,000. Candidate A's share = (45,000 ÷ 100,000) × 100 = 45%. Using 120,000 registered voters would wrongly give 37.5%, while using all votes cast including invalid votes would give about 42.9%.

questions.q: An electoral system in which seats in the legislature are distributed according to the proportion of votes won by each political party is known as
questions.explanation: Proportional representation allocates seats in relation to each party's share of the votes, often using party lists or multi-member constituencies. First-past-the-post awards a seat to the candidate with the highest votes in a constituency rather than sharing seats by party percentage.

questions.q: In a democracy, public opinion is important to a government mainly because it
options: is expressed only by members of the legislature
allows the government to ignore the constitution
helps the government to understand the feelings and preferences of the citizens
replaces the need for free and fair elections
questions.explanation: Public opinion gives rulers feedback about what citizens think and want, which can shape policies and improve accountability. It does not replace elections or constitutional rules; elected representatives and the media are among the channels through which it is expressed.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: The power of a state House of Assembly to invite the commissioner for health to explain how funds allocated to equipment procurement were spent is an example of
options: delegated legislation by a state ministry
questions.explanation: The legislature monitors executive spending and administration through invitations, committees and questions. Judicial review is carried out by courts, while delegated legislation is law-making by bodies such as ministries rather than supervision of the executive.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: Where a State House of Assembly passes a bill again by the required majority after the governor declines assent, the constitution allows the bill to become law. This procedure best illustrates
options: the supremacy of the judiciary over the legislature
the delegation of legislative power to the governor
a check by the legislature on the executive
the fusion of executive and legislative powers
questions.explanation: Overriding a veto is a legislative check on executive power because the assembly can prevent the governor's refusal from permanently blocking a bill. It does not show judicial supremacy or a fusion of executive and legislative powers.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: The security of tenure and fixed salaries of judges are constitutional devices designed mainly to
options: allow judges to make laws when parliament is not sitting
make judges members of the executive council
place the judiciary above the constitution
protect judicial independence from interference by other arms of government
questions.explanation: Security of tenure and fixed salaries reduce the risk that judges will be removed or financially pressured for deciding cases against the executive or legislature. Judges still apply the constitution and do not make laws in place of the legislature.

questions.q: Residents of a Nigerian state openly refuse to obey a new levy, insisting that the government no longer has the moral right to impose it, although tax officials attempt to enforce payment. This situation best illustrates a challenge to the government's
questions.explanation: Legitimacy concerns acceptance of a government's right to rule and make binding decisions; refusal based on moral right questions legitimacy. External sovereignty concerns independence from other states, while territorial integrity concerns the state's boundaries.

questions.q: One major reason for the creation of additional states in Nigeria after 1967 has been to
options: abolish the federal character principle in public appointments
replace the concurrent legislative list with a single national list
transfer all residual powers from the federal government to local councils
bring government closer to the people and address fears of domination by larger groups
questions.explanation: State creation has often been justified as a way to make administration more accessible and to reduce fears that one group or region would dominate others. It did not abolish federalism or transfer all residual powers to local councils.

questions.q: The ECOWAS Parliament is best described as a
options: body that appoints the President of the ECOWAS Commission
court that hears appeals from national courts of member states
consultative assembly of representatives from member states
council that fixes the common external tariff for member states
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS Parliament is a forum of representatives from member states that advises on matters affecting the community. Judicial matters are handled by the ECOWAS Court of Justice, and decisions on trade and tariff matters are not the primary responsibility of the Parliament.

questions.q: The most fundamental factor that guides Nigeria's choices in international relations is
options: the ideology of the political party in power
the personal preference of the serving foreign minister
the promotion of the country's national interest
the resolutions of the United Nations General Assembly
questions.explanation: Nigeria's foreign policy is ultimately shaped by what is considered beneficial to the country's security, economy and international standing. The views of officials, international resolutions and party ideologies may influence particular decisions, but they do not replace national interest as the fundamental guide.

questions.q: The residents of a housing estate in Port Harcourt form an association to press the state government to repair access roads, but the association does not sponsor candidates for elections. The association is best described as a
options: standing committee of the House of Assembly
questions.explanation: A pressure group seeks to influence government policy without sponsoring candidates for public office. A political party, by contrast, is organised mainly to contest elections and form or influence government.

questions.q: A professional association in Lagos presents the grievances of its members to the National Assembly and asks for a change in a proposed law. This activity is best described as
questions.explanation: Interest articulation is the process through which groups express their demands and grievances to government. The association is not selecting candidates for office, reviewing laws in court, or making subsidiary legislation.

questions.q: During campaigns, a political party in Kano explains its manifesto to traders and urges them to participate in the forthcoming elections. This best illustrates the party's role in
questions.explanation: Explaining programmes and encouraging citizens to take part in elections are ways in which parties educate and mobilise the electorate. Law-making, oversight, dispute adjudication and foreign policy formulation are performed mainly by institutions of government.

questions.q: The principle that a judge should decide cases impartially and should not be removed from office by the executive except in accordance with the constitution is known as
questions.explanation: Judicial independence protects judges from improper interference by the executive or other branches so that they can decide cases fairly. Parliamentary sovereignty concerns the supremacy of the legislature, collective responsibility relates to cabinet unity, and executive prerogative refers to certain powers of the executive.

questions.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, the power of the Senate to confirm certain appointments made by the President is an example of...
options: delegated legislation by the National Assembly
questions.explanation: The confirmation of presidential appointments by the Senate is a check by the legislature on the executive. The principle of checks and balances ensures that no organ of government exercises power without restraint.

questions.q: Which of the following legal remedies is used to challenge the unlawful detention of a person in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Habeas corpus is an order requiring a person holding another in custody to bring that person before a court to test the lawfulness of the detention. Mandamus compels an official to perform a public duty, while certiorari is used to quash a decision.

questions.q: Which military Head of State was removed from office in 1975 while attending an Organisation of African Unity summit in Kampala?
questions.explanation: General Yakubu Gowon was overthrown in July 1975 while attending an OAU summit in Kampala, Uganda. The coup brought General Murtala Mohammed to power.

questions.q: The military government that handed over power to a democratically elected government in May 1999 was headed by...
questions.explanation: General Abdulsalami Abubakar headed the military government that supervised the transition and handed over to the elected civilian government in May 1999. General Sani Abacha had died in 1998 before the handover.

questions.q: The official record containing the names of all persons qualified to vote in an election is known as the...
questions.explanation: The voters' register is the official list of persons qualified and registered to vote in an election. A voter's card is evidence of registration, while a ballot paper is used to cast the vote.

questions.q: In a ward election in Abeokuta North Local Government Area, 60,000 votes were cast. If 5,000 were invalid and a candidate scored 22,000 valid votes, what percentage of the valid votes did the candidate obtain?
questions.explanation: After removing 5,000 invalid votes, 55,000 valid votes remain. The candidate's share is (22,000 ÷ 55,000) × 100 = 40%. Using the total 60,000 votes as the denominator would wrongly give about 36.7%.

questions.q: Which of the following rights is enjoyed by a Nigerian citizen but generally not by a resident alien in Nigeria?
options: right to sue in a Nigerian court
right to vote in national elections
right to reside in the country
questions.explanation: Resident aliens may lawfully sue in court, own movable property and reside in Nigeria when their stay is valid. The right to vote in national elections is reserved for citizens.

questions.q: One lawful way by which citizens can express their opposition to a government policy is through...
options: withholding of taxes until the policy is withdrawn
destruction of government property to attract attention
peaceful procession and petition to the legislature
questions.explanation: A peaceful procession and petition to the legislature are lawful ways of expressing public opinion and seeking redress. Withholding taxes, destroying public property and disobeying court orders are unlawful acts rather than legitimate forms of protest.

questions.q: A political arrangement in which member states keep their own constitutions and final authority while the central body handles only agreed matters is best described as a
questions.explanation: A confederation is formed when sovereign member states delegate limited functions to a weak central authority while retaining final authority for themselves. A federation is different because the central government has direct constitutional authority over citizens, while a unitary system concentrates power in one central government.
